title: Southern-Style Plant-Based Enchiladas
subtitle: with Spring Onion Salsa
description: Dare we say this is the whole enchilada... because it is! It's made using plant-based mince, so it's great for vegetarians and flexitarians alike, and there's lots of smoky barbecue flavours in the sauce. Plus, it's cheesy!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Thinly slice the onion. Finely chop the tomato. Thinly slice the spring onion on an angle. Coarsely grate the cheese. Combine 1 tbs barbecue sauce, 1 tbs tomato paste and 375ml (1½ cups) water in a bowl.

Brown plant-based mince: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic, onion, plant-based mince and barbecue seasoning, breaking up the lumps with a spoon, for 4 mins or until browned. Scatter over 2 tsp plain flour and cook, stirring, for 1 min.

Simmer sauce: Add the barbecue sauce mixture to the mince and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-6 mins until thickened. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat. Put the mince mixture in a sieve over a bowl to drain, reserving the liquid.

Assemble enchiladas: Spread the reserved liquid over the base of a medium baking dish (see Kitchen 101). Divide the mince mixture among the tortillas and roll to enclose, then put in the dish, seam side down.

Bake and serve up: Scatter over the cheese and season with salt and pepper. Bake for 8-10 mins until the cheese is golden and the enchiladas are warmed through. Scatter over the tomato and spring onion, then divide among plates and enjoy.
Kitchen 101: You will need a dish large enough to fit the length of the tortillas – about 17cm x 26cm. Before filling and rolling them, trim the ends of the tortillas, if needed, to fit the dish.
